en: Romans 11

p.src: 1  I ask then, did God reject his people? May it never be! For I also am an Israelite, a descendant of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.

en: I ask then, did God reject his people? May it never be! For I also am an Israelite, a descendant of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.
u.src: 1  I ask then, did God reject his people? May it never be! For I also am an Israelite, a descendant of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.

p.src: 2  God didn’t reject his people, whom he foreknew. Or don’t you know what the Scripture says about Elijah? How he pleads with God against Israel:

en: God didn’t reject his people, whom he foreknew. Or don’t you know what the Scripture says about Elijah? How he pleads with God against Israel:
u.src: 2  God didn’t reject his people, whom he foreknew. Or don’t you know what the Scripture says about Elijah? How he pleads with God against Israel:

p.src: 3  “Lord, they have killed your prophets. They have broken down your altars. I am left alone, and they seek my life.”

en: “Lord, they have killed your prophets. They have broken down your altars. I am left alone, and they seek my life.”
u.src: 3  “Lord, they have killed your prophets. They have broken down your altars. I am left alone, and they seek my life.”

p.src: 4  But how does God answer him? “I have reserved for myself seven thousand men who have not bowed the knee to Baal.”

en: But how does God answer him? “I have reserved for myself seven thousand men who have not bowed the knee to Baal.”
u.src: 4  But how does God answer him? “I have reserved for myself seven thousand men who have not bowed the knee to Baal.”

p.src: 5  Even so too at this present time also there is a remnant according to the election of grace.

en: Even so too at this present time also there is a remnant according to the election of grace.
u.src: 5  Even so too at this present time also there is a remnant according to the election of grace.

p.src: 6  And if by grace, then it is no longer of works; otherwise grace is no longer grace. But if it is of works, it is no longer grace; otherwise work is no longer work.

en: And if by grace, then it is no longer of works; otherwise grace is no longer grace. But if it is of works, it is no longer grace; otherwise work is no longer work.
u.src: 6  And if by grace, then it is no longer of works; otherwise grace is no longer grace. But if it is of works, it is no longer grace; otherwise work is no longer work.

p.src: 7  What then? That which Israel seeks for, that he didn’t obtain, but the chosen ones obtained it, and the rest were hardened.

en: What then? That which Israel seeks for, that he didn’t obtain, but the chosen ones obtained it, and the rest were hardened.
u.src: 7  What then? That which Israel seeks for, that he didn’t obtain, but the chosen ones obtained it, and the rest were hardened.

p.src: 8  According as it is written, “God gave them a spirit of stupor, eyes that they should not see, and ears that they should not hear, to this very day.”

en: According as it is written, “God gave them a spirit of stupor, eyes that they should not see, and ears that they should not hear, to this very day.”
u.src: 8  According as it is written, “God gave them a spirit of stupor, eyes that they should not see, and ears that they should not hear, to this very day.”

en: 11:8 Deuteronomy 29:4; Isaiah 29:10

p.src: 9  David says, “Let their table be made a snare, a trap, a stumbling block, and a retribution to them.

en: David says, “Let their table be made a snare, a trap, a stumbling block, and a retribution to them.
u.src: 9  David says, “Let their table be made a snare, a trap, a stumbling block, and a retribution to them.

p.src: 10  Let their eyes be darkened, that they may not see. Always keep their backs bent.”

en: Let their eyes be darkened, that they may not see. Always keep their backs bent.”
u.src: 10  Let their eyes be darkened, that they may not see. Always keep their backs bent.”

p.src: 11  I ask then, did they stumble that they might fall? May it never be! But by their fall salvation has come to the Gentiles, to provoke them to jealousy.

en: I ask then, did they stumble that they might fall? May it never be! But by their fall salvation has come to the Gentiles, to provoke them to jealousy.
u.src: 11  I ask then, did they stumble that they might fall? May it never be! But by their fall salvation has come to the Gentiles, to provoke them to jealousy.

p.src: 12  Now if their fall is the riches of the world, and their loss the riches of the Gentiles, how much more their fullness!

en: Now if their fall is the riches of the world, and their loss the riches of the Gentiles, how much more their fullness!
u.src: 12  Now if their fall is the riches of the world, and their loss the riches of the Gentiles, how much more their fullness!

p.src: 13  For I speak to you who are Gentiles. Since then as I am an apostle to Gentiles, I glorify my ministry,

en: For I speak to you who are Gentiles. Since then as I am an apostle to Gentiles, I glorify my ministry,
u.src: 13  For I speak to you who are Gentiles. Since then as I am an apostle to Gentiles, I glorify my ministry,

p.src: 14  if by any means I may provoke to jealousy those who are my flesh, and may save some of them.

en: if by any means I may provoke to jealousy those who are my flesh, and may save some of them.
u.src: 14  if by any means I may provoke to jealousy those who are my flesh, and may save some of them.

p.src: 15  For if the rejection of them is the reconciling of the world, what would their acceptance be, but life from the dead?

en: For if the rejection of them is the reconciling of the world, what would their acceptance be, but life from the dead?
u.src: 15  For if the rejection of them is the reconciling of the world, what would their acceptance be, but life from the dead?

p.src: 16  If the first fruit is holy, so is the lump. If the root is holy, so are the branches.

en: If the first fruit is holy, so is the lump. If the root is holy, so are the branches.
u.src: 16  If the first fruit is holy, so is the lump. If the root is holy, so are the branches.

p.src: 17  But if some of the branches were broken off, and you, being a wild olive, were grafted in among them and became partaker with them of the root and of the richness of the olive tree,

en: But if some of the branches were broken off, and you, being a wild olive, were grafted in among them and became partaker with them of the root and of the richness of the olive tree,
u.src: 17  But if some of the branches were broken off, and you, being a wild olive, were grafted in among them and became partaker with them of the root and of the richness of the olive tree,

p.src: 18  don’t boast over the branches. But if you boast, remember that it is not you who support the root, but the root supports you.

en: don’t boast over the branches. But if you boast, remember that it is not you who support the root, but the root supports you.
u.src: 18  don’t boast over the branches. But if you boast, remember that it is not you who support the root, but the root supports you.

p.src: 19  You will say then, “Branches were broken off, that I might be grafted in.”

en: You will say then, “Branches were broken off, that I might be grafted in.”
u.src: 19  You will say then, “Branches were broken off, that I might be grafted in.”

p.src: 20  True; by their unbelief they were broken off, and you stand by your faith. Don’t be conceited, but fear;

en: True; by their unbelief they were broken off, and you stand by your faith. Don’t be conceited, but fear;
u.src: 20  True; by their unbelief they were broken off, and you stand by your faith. Don’t be conceited, but fear;

p.src: 21  for if God didn’t spare the natural branches, neither will he spare you.

en: for if God didn’t spare the natural branches, neither will he spare you.
u.src: 21  for if God didn’t spare the natural branches, neither will he spare you.

p.src: 22  See then the goodness and severity of God. Toward those who fell, severity; but toward you, goodness, if you continue in his goodness; otherwise you also will be cut off.

en: See then the goodness and severity of God. Toward those who fell, severity; but toward you, goodness, if you continue in his goodness; otherwise you also will be cut off.
u.src: 22  See then the goodness and severity of God. Toward those who fell, severity; but toward you, goodness, if you continue in his goodness; otherwise you also will be cut off.

p.src: 23  They also, if they don’t continue in their unbelief, will be grafted in, for God is able to graft them in again.

en: They also, if they don’t continue in their unbelief, will be grafted in, for God is able to graft them in again.
u.src: 23  They also, if they don’t continue in their unbelief, will be grafted in, for God is able to graft them in again.

p.src: 24  For if you were cut out of that which is by nature a wild olive tree, and were grafted contrary to nature into a good olive tree, how much more will these, which are the natural branches, be grafted into their own olive tree?

en: For if you were cut out of that which is by nature a wild olive tree, and were grafted contrary to nature into a good olive tree, how much more will these, which are the natural branches, be grafted into their own olive tree?
u.src: 24  For if you were cut out of that which is by nature a wild olive tree, and were grafted contrary to nature into a good olive tree, how much more will these, which are the natural branches, be grafted into their own olive tree?

p.src: 25  For I don’t desire you to be ignorant, brothers, of this mystery, so that you won’t be wise in your own conceits, that a partial hardening has happened to Israel, until the fullness of the Gentiles has come in,

en: For I don’t desire you to be ignorant, brothers, of this mystery, so that you won’t be wise in your own conceits, that a partial hardening has happened to Israel, until the fullness of the Gentiles has come in,
u.src: 25  For I don’t desire you to be ignorant, brothers, of this mystery, so that you won’t be wise in your own conceits, that a partial hardening has happened to Israel, until the fullness of the Gentiles has come in,

en: 11:25 The word for “brothers” here and where context allows may also be correctly translated “brothers and sisters” or “siblings.”

p.src: 26  and so all Israel will be saved. Even as it is written, “There will come out of Zion the Deliverer, and he will turn away ungodliness from Jacob.

en: and so all Israel will be saved. Even as it is written, “There will come out of Zion the Deliverer, and he will turn away ungodliness from Jacob.
u.src: 26  and so all Israel will be saved. Even as it is written, “There will come out of Zion the Deliverer, and he will turn away ungodliness from Jacob.

p.src: 27  This is my covenant with them, when I will take away their sins.”

en: This is my covenant with them, when I will take away their sins.”
u.src: 27  This is my covenant with them, when I will take away their sins.”

p.src: 28  Concerning the Good News, they are enemies for your sake. But concerning the election, they are beloved for the fathers’ sake.

en: Concerning the Good News, they are enemies for your sake. But concerning the election, they are beloved for the fathers’ sake.
u.src: 28  Concerning the Good News, they are enemies for your sake. But concerning the election, they are beloved for the fathers’ sake.

en: For the gifts and the calling of God are irrevocable.

u.src: 30  For as you in time past were disobedient to God, but now have obtained mercy by their disobedience,

en: For God has bound all to disobedience, that he might have mercy on all.
